name: Pitztaler Gletscher
kurzbeschreibung: The Pitztal Glacier is Tyrol's rooftop: Wildspitzbahn to Café 3440 at 3,440 meters, eternal ice, and panoramas over 50 three-thousand-meter peaks.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental, ice-clad Pitztal Glacier crowns the head of the Pitztal valley at elevations reaching 3,440 meters, rightfully known as the spectacular 'Rooftop of Tyrol.' As Austria's highest glaciated ski domain and highest cable car destination, this primordial ice realm unfolds across the massive Mittelbergferner and neighboring Taschachferner glaciers in pristine alpine glory. The majestic Wildspitze – at 3,768 meters the highest summit in North Tyrol and the second highest mountain in Austria – presides over the glaciated landscape. An architectural masterpiece and centerpiece of the destination is the futuristic Café 3440 at the mountain terminus of the Wildspitzbahn: With its cantilevered glass observation deck, the building floats weightlessly over the glacial abyss, providing an unrestricted 360-degree panorama over more than fifty glaciated three-thousand-meter peaks across the Ötztal Alps.

Route & Requirements

Ascending into this high-alpine ice world is a technical and scenic adventure of the highest caliber: First, the subterranean Pitzexpress funicular pierces through solid rock for over three kilometers up to the mountain station at 2,840 meters. From there, the ultra-modern Wildspitzbahn gondola glides swiftly to the observation deck at 3,440 meters. The entire summit complex, including Café 3440, is barrier-free. For experienced mountaineers, the glacier is the starting point for classic ascents of the Wildspitze (approx. 3.5 hours, crampons, ice axes, and rope team mandatory). A rewarding family-friendly option is the glacier path descending toward the Braunschweiger Hütte. Sturdy mountaineering boots, warm thermal clothing, and category 4 sunglasses are essential due to intense high-altitude UV radiation.

Visit & Arrival

The base station at Mittelberg in the rear Pitztal provides spacious free parking and is reached via the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Imst-Pitztal) and the L16 provincial road. Rail travelers journey to Imst-Pitztal railway station and take the direct Regiobus Pitztal (line 4204), which stops right outside the Pitzexpress station.

Tips

Order a cappuccino and homemade Tyrolean buckwheat cake on the cantilevered panorama deck of Café 3440 while gazing down into deep ice chasms. Take a quiet moment at the architecturally unique Chapel of White Light, situated near the glacier edge for peaceful contemplation amidst immense mountain giants.
preis: Glacier area accessible; Pitzexpress and Wildspitzbahn cable cars chargeable (Glacier ticket)
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily mid-July to mid-May (brief maintenance break in early summer)
